scope: Mechanism synthesis of the existing seven-note C. elegans embryonic morphogenesis series; no literature expansion.

priorities.P1: Overview rewritten around effective deformation, direction selection, and shape retention. Developmental notes 01–05 separated from cross-cutting notes 06–07; imaging/genetic basics follow the synthesis.
priorities.P2: 02 adds contact capacity and loading schedules, then a two-state material example with matched shape, total stress and initial strain rate. 03 compares present drive, tangent stiffness and inherited state.
priorities.P3: 04 distinguishes evidential status of actin remodeling and cadherin trafficking; mechanical series/parallel configurations are separated from kinetic dependency and phase division.
priorities.P4: 06 leads with rigidity loss, active barrier crossing and identity-directed rearrangement; adjacency remains core, nematic defects and persistent homology move to expanded reading.
priorities.other_notes: 01 connects drive, transfer and geometry; 05 compares active bending, contact and reference curvature; 07 maps microscopic network variables to surface stress, tangent stiffness, relaxation and reference state.

evidence_boundaries: All new constitutive examples explicitly labeled as candidate models, without fitted embryo parameters.
No assignment of permanent junction reference strain to the published Yang model; its concentration–line-tension feedback is distinguished from that hypothesis.
Mechanical series geometry does not imply both molecular update paths are required; length fractions retained in serial strain formula.
History denotes present internal variables, not an independent force from past events.
Cadherin fluorescence is not assumed to measure force or number of load-bearing units.
